title: MAP: A Model-agnostic Pretraining Framework for Click-through Rate Prediction

problem.claim: CTR prediction must learn from multi-field categorical data and very large volumes of user interaction logs, but supervised click signals may be insufficient for learning capable feature and instance representations.

gap.claim: Self-supervised learning for CTR prediction remains an open question because existing work is preliminary and rudimentary.

contributions.claim: The MAP framework applies feature corruption and recovery to multi-field categorical data for CTR pretraining.
Masked feature prediction uses masking, feature prediction, and Noise Contrastive Estimation to model feature interactions within instances and handle large feature spaces.
Replaced feature detection converts the pretraining task into binary classification by replacing and detecting changed input features.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the Avazu and Criteo datasets, the authors report advantages over several strong baselines.
The authors report new state-of-the-art performance and efficiency for CTR prediction.

narrative_sequence.summary: CTR prediction is important in online advertising and involves multi-field categorical data at very large scale.
Supervised click signals may not fully support learning capable representations, motivating self-supervised pretraining.
Existing self-supervised CTR work is preliminary, leaving the area open.
MAP introduces corruption-and-recovery pretraining through MFP and RFD.
Experiments on Avazu and Criteo are reported to outperform strong baselines in performance and efficiency.

unknowns: Exact dataset sizes, preprocessing, and train-validation-test splits are not specified.
Baseline identities, metric values, statistical significance, and ablation results are not specified.
Model configurations, computational cost, and implementation or reproducibility details are not specified.
Generalization beyond CTR prediction and the two reported datasets is not established.
